mechanism: Map the given diagonal cut to D's rising hole side and the packet bottom fold boundary to D's horizontal hole base. This targets stopping after a single unfold instead of both perpendicular reflections.
marker_roles: Red dashed original cut identifies the actual diagonal operation, with dashes unchanged.
Red rising side of D triangle is the false cut-output correspondence.
Blue bottom packet fold edge identifies an actual folding boundary.
Blue horizontal base of D hole is the false persistence of the crease as final cut boundary; existing triangle contour only.
primary_math_proof: The closed packet has crease boundaries right x=1 and bottom y=0, open stacked edges top/left. In local quarter[0,1]^2, cut endpoints(.5,0),(1,.5) remove the corner triangle at(1,0). Reflections(x,y),(2-x,y),(x,-y),(2-x,-y) give diamond vertices(.5,0),(1,.5),(1.5,0),(1,-.5), strictly interior to original[0,2]×[-1,1]. OnlyE has this hole. D omits the final reflection andC has axis-aligned edges. Original dashedcut, fold/open edges, all fills and choices retained.
